payload.task_text:
Our investment team needs to compile the weekly market analysis report. A financial analytics dashboard is available at http://localhost:30204/dashboard.html that displays sector performance indices, weekly returns, year-to-date returns, volatility levels, and analyst consensus ratings for five market sectors: Communication Services, Consumer Cyclical, Financial Services, Healthcare, and Energy.

We also track five individual stocks that represent these sectors: GOOGL for Communication Services, AMZN for Consumer Cyclical, JPM for Financial Services, JNJ for Healthcare, and XOM for Energy. We need to cross-reference sector-level performance with individual stock data.

Please browse the market dashboard and extract all sector performance data including weekly return, sector index value, YTD return, volatility level, analyst consensus rating, and target price upside for each of the five sectors.

Then retrieve the current stock data for each of the five tickers (GOOGL, AMZN, JPM, JNJ, XOM) from the financial data service. For each stock, get the current price, sector, market capitalization, P/E ratio, and dividend yield.

Create a Google Sheet called "Weekly_Market_Analysis" with two sheets. The first sheet called "Sector Performance" should have columns Sector, Weekly_Return, Sector_Index, YTD_Return, Volatility, Consensus, and Target_Upside, with one row for each of the five sectors. The second sheet called "Stock vs Sector" should have columns Ticker, Stock_Price, Sector, Market_Cap_B (market cap in billions, rounded to 1 decimal), PE_Ratio, Dividend_Yield_Pct, Sector_Weekly_Return, and Sector_YTD_Return. Map each stock to its corresponding sector data from the dashboard.

Next, create a Word document called "Weekly_Market_Report.docx" in the workspace as an executive summary. Include a title, a market overview paragraph, a section for each sector discussing the sector index performance alongside the representative stock, and a conclusion identifying the best and worst performing sectors of the week ranked by weekly return (the sector with the highest weekly return is the best; the sector with the lowest weekly return is the worst, even if it is positive).

Finally, send an email to committee@investmentfirm.com with the subject "Weekly Market Analysis Report" (the sender address is fixed by the email environment, so just use your default account). The body should highlight the top performing sector and any sectors with negative weekly returns.

Save all output files to the workspace directory.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. The stock calls are tiny, while delegated browser work adds no useful dependency. First freeze the task-visible agent-workspace absolute path from the Visible Boundary/current working directory; never assume `/workspace`.

In one orchestration response, call `mcp__playwright_with_chunk__browser_navigate` exactly once for `http://localhost:30204/dashboard.html` and issue the five Yahoo Finance stock-info calls for `GOOGL`, `AMZN`, `JPM`, `JNJ`, and `XOM` natively in parallel. If navigation succeeds, call `browser_snapshot` exactly once and extract the five named sector rows. Do not call `browser_install`, Terminal, PDF, Word-browser helpers, email-browser helpers, alternate URLs, or any unrelated tool while acquiring sources; on a navigation/snapshot failure, report the exact source blocker and do not guess dashboard values.

Require exactly five complete sector rows `{sector,weekly_return,sector_index,ytd_return,volatility,consensus,target_upside}` and five complete stock rows `{ticker,current_price,sector,market_cap,pe_ratio,dividend_yield}`. Freeze one literal canonical five-row stock-sector join, including raw-return best/worst sectors and market cap converted to billions once. From only that payload, the main agent creates exactly one `Weekly_Market_Analysis` Google spreadsheet and `<agent_workspace>/Weekly_Market_Report.docx`, using the task's exact sheets, columns, sections, mapping, and rounding, and sends one email to `committee@investmentfirm.com` with subject `Weekly Market Analysis Report`. Read each output once and reconcile it to the same payload; do not add sent-mail discovery, browser retries, diagnostic writes, or a verification wave.

Create a Word document at this exact absolute path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-playwright-yf-market-dashboard-gsheet-word/workspace/Weekly_Market_Report.docx

CONTEXT: This is an executive summary for an investment committee, covering five market sectors and one representative stock per sector. All data below is final and verified — use it exactly as given, do not invent or alter any numbers.

DOCUMENT STRUCTURE (required, in this order):
1. Title (Heading level 1): "Weekly Market Analysis Report"
2. A short metadata line (plain paragraph): "Report Period: March 1-7, 2026 | Data Sources: Market Analytics Pro Dashboard and Yahoo Finance"
3. Heading "Market Overview" + the overview paragraph given below
4. Five sector sections, each with a heading and one paragraph (headings and paragraphs given below)
5. Heading "Conclusion" + the conclusion paragraph given below

Required headings for the five sector sections (use Heading level 2):
- "Communication Services (Representative Stock: GOOGL)"
- "Consumer Cyclical (Representative Stock: AMZN)"
- "Financial Services (Representative Stock: JPM)"
- "Healthcare (Representative Stock: JNJ)"
- "Energy (Representative Stock: XOM)"

--- TEXT CONTENT (use verbatim) ---

MARKET OVERVIEW paragraph:
During the March 1-7, 2026 reporting period, four of the five tracked sectors posted positive weekly returns, with Energy leading at +3.1% and Communication Services close behind at +2.8%. Consumer Cyclical was the only sector to decline, finishing the week at -1.2%. On a year-to-date basis, Energy (+15.2%) and Communication Services (+12.4%) remain the clear leaders, while Healthcare continues to lag with a -2.1% year-to-date return and the lowest sector index reading of the group at 98.7. Volatility is concentrated in Energy and Communication Services, both classified as High, while Healthcare offers the lowest volatility profile. Analyst sentiment is constructive across the board: Energy and Communication Services carry Strong Buy consensus ratings with the largest target price upside (+22.1% and +18.5% respectively), Financial Services and Consumer Cyclical are rated Buy, and Healthcare is the only sector at Hold with a more modest +5.2% upside.

COMMUNICATION SERVICES paragraph:
The Communication Services sector index closed the week at 118.5, gaining +2.8% and extending its year-to-date advance to +12.4%. Volatility remains High, but analysts maintain a Strong Buy consensus with an average target price upside of +18.5% across 42 covering analysts. Representative stock Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) trades at $300.88, giving it a market capitalization of roughly $3,639.7 billion, the largest of the five representative names. The stock changes hands at a trailing P/E of 27.81 and offers a modest 0.28% dividend yield, reflecting a growth-oriented profile consistent with the sector's high-volatility, high-upside character.

CONSUMER CYCLICAL paragraph:
Consumer Cyclical was the week's only declining sector, with its index slipping to 105.3 for a -1.2% weekly return. The sector's year-to-date gain of +5.7% is the second weakest in the group, and volatility is classified as Medium. Analysts nonetheless maintain a Buy consensus with +12.3% average target price upside across 38 analysts. Representative stock Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) trades at $218.94 with a market capitalization of approximately $2,350.3 billion. At a trailing P/E of 30.49, the richest valuation among the five representative names, and with no dividend paid, Amazon's profile reflects the discretionary, growth-driven nature of the sector.

FINANCIAL SERVICES paragraph:
The Financial Services sector index finished at 112.8, up +1.5% for the week and +8.9% year to date, with Medium volatility. Analysts rate the sector a Buy with +9.8% average target price upside across 35 analysts. Representative stock JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM) trades at $293.55 with a market capitalization of about $791.7 billion. The stock's trailing P/E of 14.66 is the lowest of the five representative names, and its 2.00% dividend yield is among the higher yields in the group, a combination that anchors the sector's relatively steady, income-generating profile.

HEALTHCARE paragraph:
Healthcare posted a marginal +0.3% weekly gain, with its sector index at 98.7, the lowest reading of the five sectors. The sector remains in negative territory year to date at -2.1%, making it the only sector with a negative year-to-date return. Volatility is Low, the most defensive profile in the group, and analysts hold a Hold consensus with +5.2% average target price upside across 30 analysts, the most cautious stance of the five sectors. Representative stock Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) trades at $239.63 with a market capitalization of approximately $577.5 billion, a trailing P/E of 21.71, and a 2.12% dividend yield, consistent with the sector's low-volatility, income-oriented character.

ENERGY paragraph:
Energy was the week's standout performer, with its sector index climbing to 122.4, the highest of the five sectors, for a +3.1% weekly return. The sector also leads on a year-to-date basis at +15.2%. Volatility is High, and analysts are the most constructive here, with a Strong Buy consensus and the largest average target price upside of the group at +22.1% across 28 analysts. Representative stock Exxon Mobil Corporation (XOM) trades at $150.76 with a market capitalization of roughly $628.2 billion. The stock carries a trailing P/E of 22.50 and the highest dividend yield of the five representative names at 2.75%, pairing the sector's strong momentum with meaningful income.

CONCLUSION paragraph:
Ranked by weekly return, Energy was the best performing sector of the week at +3.1%, followed by Communication Services (+2.8%), Financial Services (+1.5%), Healthcare (+0.3%), and Consumer Cyclical (-1.2%). Consumer Cyclical was the worst performing sector of the week and the only one to post a negative weekly return, even as its year-to-date result remains positive. Energy's leadership is corroborated by the strongest year-to-date return (+15.2%), the highest sector index (122.4), and the most bullish analyst consensus (Strong Buy with +22.1% target price upside), while Consumer Cyclical's pullback stands in contrast to its still-positive year-to-date gain and Buy consensus.

--- END TEXT CONTENT ---

FORMATTING NOTES:
- Use Heading level 1 for the title and the "Market Overview"/"Conclusion" headings, Heading level 2 for the five sector sections.
- Ensure every paragraph is present and non-empty.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA / DELIVERABLE:
After writing, verify by calling mcp__word__get_document_text (and mcp__word__get_document_outline) on the file. Confirm all 5 sector sections, the title, the market overview, and the conclusion are present.
Report back: the absolute file path, the number of headings/paragraphs, the outline, and confirmation that every section listed above appears in the extracted text.
